reason: The mechanism is real and the consequence built on it is not, and the fix is wrong three ways. Driven in chromium at 1440/1280/768/390, light and dark, reducedMotion, at ?state=partial and ?state=full. Confirmed: the band head prints the typed literal 'All five counted out of 9' (lately.html:861, hardcoded, state-blind), the row holds 5 .kpi (1 .lead + 4 status), 1 carries .na and no meter, 3 carry meters, and .kpi.lead .sr speaks the unconditional 'Every card in this row is counted out of these 9 open jobs.' (lately.html:756). So the word 'five' is loose by one in exactly one state. Everything the finding derives from that is wrong. (1) The consequence assumes the cards are parts of a whole - 'is the missing due-date count included in the nine or not?' There is nothing to include. D.open is F.bound.openCount, a Tasks-derived bound figure the build gates; the four status cards are overlapping subsets of it, not addends. In full the row reads 3, 2, 1, 0 against 9 - the numbers already do not sum, and no reader is summing them. Whether Timeline answered cannot move the nine, so the question the owner is said to be stuck on has no bearing on any figure on the screen and the shared-denominator claim is untouched: every card that has a reading is still read against the same 9. (2) 'they must decide which to believe' does not survive the frame. Screenshotted at 1440, the stamp is tracked uppercase mono, dim, flush right in the band head - a scale legend, not a headline - and the card 27px under it prints an em-dash rule where a numeral goes, no meter, and the words NOT AVAILABLE, with a note directly beneath the row reading 'Timeline did not answer this reading, so nothing here knows a due date. The card keeps its place and says so; it does not fall back to zero.' The fact is stated three times in ink before any reader reaches an ambiguity. The honest-degradation contract is 'a reader can never mistake we-don't-know for it's-zero'; nothing here offers a zero or any number to mistake. (3) The one measurement offered is wrong at every width driven: the label's bottom sits 27px above the unavailable card at 1440 and 1280, and 166px/169px at 390/768 where the row stacks. 'Forty pixels below' matches no width. Severity is overstated on top of that. defect requires something visibly wrong; what is visible is a legend that says five where four carry readings, corrected in ink twice within one card-height. That is refinement, and an overstated class is itself a reason to refute. The fix is worse than the looseness. (a) It puts three numerals into the row's only denominator declaration - 'Four of five counted out of 9' - so the stamp whose whole job is to name the one shared base now invites the part-of-whole arithmetic that does not exist, and demotes a protected object to a caveat about card availability. (b) The sr rewrite re-opens a closed round-2 finding. kpi-cards-announce-their-fact-twice moved the row's sentence onto the group's own name so each card is announced once; the unavailability already exists in the tree exactly once, on the NA card's aria-label 'Jobs past the day they were due: not available, because Timeline did not answer'. Appending '; the due-date card was not read.' to the lead card's sr announces it a second time in the tree and a fourth time on the surface. (c) Its arithmetic never matches its own output: `const counted = 4 - (partial ? 1 : 0)` counts status cards, so counted is 3 in partial and 4 in full, then it prints 'Four of five' when counted is 3 and 'All five' when counted is 4 - the variable equals the printed number in neither branch. And it does not do the thing it advertises: 'derive the label from the row rather than typing it' is delivered as two more typed strings keyed off the same `partial` boolean that already drives `unavailable`. Nothing is read from the row.
sharpenedFix:
If anything is done here at all - and it is a one-word refinement on a legend, not a defect - do it without putting a second count in front of the denominator and without saying the same thing a fourth time. Two options, both cheap. Preferred: make the stamp state-independent by dropping the card count from it entirely - replace lately.html:861 with `

Counted out of ${D.open}

`. It is true in every state including any future one where a second source fails, it keeps the shared denominator as the only number in the legend, it needs no flag threaded into movementTwo, and it drops one word rather than adding four. Second best, if the five is felt to be load-bearing: derive it from what was actually rendered rather than from the flag - build the four status cards into an array first, count the ones rendered with a meter, and print `${n} of five counted out of ${D.open}` with n spelled as a word. Leave leadKpi alone in both cases: the lead card's sr should say 'Every card in this row that carries a number is counted out of these 9 open jobs.' at most - one clause, state-independent, no second mention of the due-date card, whose own aria-label already carries the reason.
breaks: Taking the seat's fix as written would regress kpi-cards-announce-their-fact-twice (r2) in the accessibility tree and add a state-dependent branch to a label that is currently one literal, a drift source nothing gates. If the sharpened 'Counted out of 9' is taken instead, re-measure: audit.mjs for the label ramp, tracking and leading on .band-head .t-label (the stamp shortens by two words, so the flex-wrap point in the band head moves and must be checked at 390, 768 and 1280 where the head already wraps); interaction-check.mjs for any assertion matching the old string - grep /All five|counted out of/ before landing, currently no assertion matches, which is itself worth noting since the row's denominator legend is ungated; and re-shoot full, partial, first-run and loading, since movementTwo renders inside .sk-wrap in loading and the stamp's width there sets the skeleton head geometry.
